function: Multi-agent DQN controls per-subcarrier transmit power, sub-band, user association and subcarrier allocation of fixed-wing UAV aerial base stations to maximize cumulative throughput (p. 7-8).
system: M=3 single-antenna fixed-wing UAV base stations, N=2000 single-antenna ground users, no RIS; 30 MHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated (p. 2, 10).
method: Multi-agent deep Q-network (DQN), reinforcement learning with replay memory and epsilon-greedy; trajectory from ARIMA prediction plus K-Means clustering, not learned (p. 5, 7).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician air-ground channel with fading power from [28], RVGM group mobility of users, Dubins flight model; online RL in simulation, no dataset (p. 3-4, 10).
test_conditions: Agents train online in the simulator for 200 episodes; evaluation sweeps FW-UAV speed (40-90 m/s), maximum power and subcarriers per UAV; no unseen scenario (p. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: convex-optimization (COM) scheme. Variants of own scheme with a simple rule: random user association, average power split. No earlier learned method compared (p. 10).
metrics: Cumulative throughput, reward, MSE loss of the Q-network, SINR coverage maps and effective coverage region (p. 10-13).
complexity: O(Ns^3 + Nin M N + Nt M K Nep Nst Nsl) for the full scheme, versus convex optimization O(Lmax log(1/Delta)(M K N Nt)^3.5) (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 4: "it is more accurate to adopt the Rician fading model"; custom Rician air-ground model with constants from [28], [34] (p. 10); no 3GPP, measured or ray-tracing channel is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "operates as an online learning scheme"; p. 11-12 only sweep the UAV speed, maximum power and subcarriers, with no test of a trained model in an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 10: "the random access scheme, the average power scheme, and the convex optimization method (COM)-based scheme are adopted as the benchmark schemes"; COM is non-learned, the other two replace one decision of the proposed scheme by a simple rule, and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the proposed MA-DRLbased joint optimization scheme is O(Ns3 + Nfe Nin M N + Nt M KNep Nst Nsl )"
q5_support: p. 10: "is demonstrated by numerical simulation"; the channel is simulated (p. 4) and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included in area 6: the DQN learns transmit power, sub-band, user association and subcarrier allocation for aerial base stations (p. 7-8), a physical-layer decision in an aerial link, learned jointly with user association. The trajectory is not learned: ARIMA, K-Means and Dubins geometry (p. 5-7). The random-access and average-power benchmarks replace one decision of the scheme by a simple rule and are drawn as learning curves in Fig. 6(c) (p. 10), so I treated them as ablations; the reviewer can confirm q3 on p. 10 and in Fig. 8 (p. 11). Carrier frequency is not stated.
